body:
N-26 SLICES 1 AND 2 ARE BUILT, NOT WALKED, NOT MARKED (helper-n26, 15 Nov 2026). The item is not complete (slices 3 to 5 and N-28 remain; RELEASE-CANDIDATE 4b needs 1 and 2 in the first public image: both are built). I did not run `roadmap.py mark`.

SLICE 1 AMENDMENT (found on the real stack by the lead, 14 Nov): two REMOVED UPLOADS (Nneka - Heartbeat, Foals - Full Performance, videoType None, isAvailable False, no album, artists [KEXP]) were filed under KEXP because the reader took "no videoType and unavailable" for a removed catalogue song. Only an ALBUM says that now; unavailable proves nothing. Recorded (tests/fixtures/ytm/n26/kexp_removed_uploads.get_playlist.json), tests seen red first, invariant over every recorded upload.

SLICE 2 (migration 0014, song_ref.artist_basis + uploader, nullable, NOTHING else: no default/check/update):
- NULL = "as before" = a performer, NEVER `channel`. Old rows, phone/file/scan refs keep NULL. Value checked in refs (a 5th basis needs no table rebuild). Not sent to phones (docs/17 unchanged, tested).
- Set by the importer only (refs.resolve keyword arguments; a client's artistBasis/uploader is ignored at POST refs/resolve and at the file import, tested). A nameless song is `unknown` whatever the reader says.
- FACTS ARE ONLY FILLED, NEVER REWRITTEN (refs.facts_to_fill, one rule for _enrich and the merge repair): the design says only "fills a null basis only when the artist agrees"; a set basis is never changed by a stronger or weaker reading (upgrade = slice 5 / N-28, with the artist rewrite). Basis fills only when the reading names the same artist; `channel`/`unknown` only when the ref plays from the very video the reading came from (a performer's catalogue ref found by name for an upload on the band's own channel must not be downgraded). The uploader is a fact about the VIDEO, stored with its video id, filled whatever the artist (slice 5 recognises a ref filed under its channel by stored artist == stored uploader).
- refmerge: both columns in _NOT_COPIED, same rule (basis follows the artist, uploader follows the video).
- artist_finder: a name is asked about only with its performer/NULL songs; all channel/unknown = skipped, nothing remembered. cover_finder: channel/unknown songs are left out of the pass (the lead's "never"; COST: a band's own-channel upload loses a catalogue cover until N-28 and keeps its video thumbnail; ONE line to overrule: the performer_clause in _wanting) and the placeholder NAME `[Unknown Artist]` (the scan's refs, no facts) is not sent either. SQL is (col IS NULL OR col NOT IN ...): a bare NOT IN drops every NULL row.

STILL OPEN: slice 3 (no artist page for a channel: proof on the real music server first), slice 4 (shapes of context: ARTE Concert, Crunchyroll), slice 5 (repair of stored rows, trigger-gated), N-28 (catalogue names the artist of a `channel` song). Known leftovers, all pinned by named tests: an OMV credited to a label with no separator keeps the label; an upload whose title names nobody keeps its uploader flagged `channel`; a description with the placeholder and NO id is a new ref each time (nothing in the server makes one repeatedly).
